findings.claim: Multi-turn tool use is hard-broken (HTTP 400) on every Gemini 3.x model: the journal replay rebuilds functionCall parts without the thoughtSignature Gemini issued, which Gemini 3 validates as required.
findings.evidence: LIVE PROBE (GOOGLE_API_KEY via infisical): a 2-turn tool loop `client "google/gemini-3.5-flash"` + `tools [weather_probe]` fails on the second request with 400: "Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts. This is required for tools to work correctly... Please refer to https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures". The identical loop on gemini-2.5-flash succeeds ("The weather in NYC is sunny."). Root cause chain: response side, `GmRespPart.thoughtSignature` is declared (ns_internal/gemini.baml:177) but `google_parse` (:693-743) never reads it and `ai.content.ToolUse` has no field to carry it; request side, `GmFunctionCall` (:33-36) and `GmPart` (:45-101) have no thoughtSignature field, so `google_lower_journal` (:505-511) replays `functionCall` bare. Not covered by PLAN §6 (which defers only streaming tool-call *deltas*) — this kills non-streaming tool use on all current-generation Gemini models (only the legacy 2.x default still works).
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the signature: add `thoughtSignature: string?` to GmPart/GmFunctionCall-part construction, surface it from google_parse (e.g. a metadata slot on ai.content.ToolUse or a google-private side map keyed by the synthesized call id inside the journal's AssistantMessage), and re-attach it in google_lower_journal when the replaying client_id matches. Also capture thoughtSignature from streamed fragments when streaming tool calls land.

findings.claim: Both Google backends fetch and base64-inline every http(s) media URL (`resolve_media(media, true)`), losing Vertex's URL-passthrough (`fileData.fileUri`) semantics — a regression vs sys_llm's Vertex defaults and a break for YouTube-URL video input on both backends.
findings.evidence: PROBE probe_media_url_vertex: an image `from_url(http://...)` lowered through `google.internal.vertex_render` produces `inlineData` (inline=true|file=false), never `fileData`. PROBE probe_media_youtube: `baml.media.Video.from_url("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ")` is live-FETCHED and the watch-page HTML is inlined as base64 `inlineData` (inline=true|file=false) with a guessed video mime — garbage on the wire, though YouTube URLs are a documented Gemini `fileData.fileUri` input (https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content FileData). Ground truth: sys_llm Vertex defaults were `send_url_add_mime_type`/`send_url` (crates/sys_llm/src/baml_std.rs:331-338 — URLs pass through), and resolve_media.rs:175-177 shows only SendBase64* strategies fetch; the native `_gm_media_part` (ns_internal/gemini.baml:368-377) hardcodes fetch_url=true for both GoogleClient and VertexClient (vertex.baml:249-266 reuses gemini_build_body). Also subjects Vertex media to the inline request-size cap where a URL would have streamed server-side.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass fetch_url=false (URL passthrough) for the Vertex backend per sys_llm defaults, and special-case YouTube URLs (and Files-API URIs) as fileData on the Developer API backend rather than fetching them.

findings.claim: A response with no candidates/content (e.g. `{}` from a broken proxy or quota edge) parses as a successful Complete turn with empty content, so a `-> string` function silently returns "" instead of erroring — sys_llm and the engine both raised an error here.
findings.evidence: PROBE probe_empty_parse: google_parse over `{}` yields `0|Complete|<null>`. PROBE probe_empty_e2e: a mock returning body `{}` makes `ai.Agent<string>.run(...).value` return the empty string as a normal success (`value=[]`) — no ParseFailed, no NoContent. Ground truth: sys_llm requires exactly one candidate else `NoContent` (crates/sys_llm/src/parse_response/google.rs:80-88) and errors on missing `content` (:92-97); engine google/vertex response_handlers do the same (research §5.1). This divergence is in the research matrix but is NOT in PLAN §5's accepted-divergence table or §6 deferrals. `google_parse` takes `resp.candidates?.at(0)` (ns_internal/gemini.baml:697) and tolerates absence everywhere.
findings.suggested_fix: In google_parse (and the stream decoder's end-state), throw ai.errors.ParseFailed (or Refused when promptFeedback.blockReason is set) when the response has neither candidates content, a blockReason, nor an error object.

findings.claim: Malformed/truncated SSE payloads are silently swallowed (catch_all → null) and a stream that ends without any finishReason finalizes as a successful Complete turn — so a connection cut mid-answer yields a silently truncated partial answer presented as success.
findings.evidence: PROBE probe_sse_malformed: SSE events [valid fragment "po", truncated JSON fragment `{"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"text":"ng`] make `stream.final()` return `final=[po]` — no error, no MaxTokens/incomplete signal; TurnStream.final_turn defaults stop_reason to Complete (ai/ns_stream:235 `self._stop_reason ?? Complete`). Code: `_gm_decode_batch` drops undecodable `data:` payloads via `catch_all (e) { _ => null }` (ns_internal/gemini.baml:799-801) and only emits a stop reason when `finishReason != ""` (:825-833). Gemini's SSE has no terminal sentinel (comment :793-794), so decoder-level leniency plus the Complete default means truncation is undetectable by the caller. Contrast: the 4xx/5xx and mid-stream `{"error":...}` paths are handled correctly (probes: 400→InvalidRequest, 429→RateLimited, 503→NetworkFailure; mid-stream error payload → RateLimited).
findings.suggested_fix: Track whether a finishReason was ever seen in the decode state; on stream end without one (or on an undecodable fragment), raise a classified failure (NetworkFailure with detail "stream ended before finishReason") instead of finalizing Complete.

findings.claim: The sys_llm `enterprise` backend switch (`enterprise` option / `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE` / `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI` flipping a google client to the Vertex backend, google-genai SDK parity) is absent from the native google package, while the shipped keyword docs still document it.
findings.evidence: grep over crates/baml_builtins2/baml_std/google/ finds no `enterprise` or `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE` handling; `GoogleClient` (google/gemini.baml:26-144) has no such option and `google_render`/`_google_request` never consult those env vars. Ground truth: sys_llm rewrites GoogleAi→VertexAi on the option or either env var (crates/sys_llm/src/build_request/mod.rs:41-57,78-83); research §6.16 lists the switch as blocking for parity; google-genai README documents `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE` (fetched). Not listed in PLAN §5 or §6. Additionally crates/baml_builtins2/keyword_docs/baml_keywords.yaml:221-241 still tells users `options.enterprise = true` / `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=true` works — stale either way. Likely an intentional design simplification (explicit VertexClient), but it is an undocumented drop: needs either implementation or an explicit deferral entry + keyword-docs update.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide explicitly: either honor GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE/GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI at request time in GoogleClient (delegating to a VertexClient built from the same options), or add the drop to PLAN §6 and rewrite the google-ai/vertex-ai keyword_docs entries for the native client surface.

findings.claim: Claude-on-Vertex rawPredict body includes `model`, which current docs explicitly say is not passed in the request body (it lives in the URL).
findings.evidence: platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-on-vertex-ai: "On Agent Platform, `model` is not passed in the request body. Instead, it is specified in the Google Cloud endpoint URL." `_vertex_anthropic_body` (ns_internal/vertex.baml:214-235) passes `model: c.model` into anthropic.internal.AnthropicBodyParams, and anthropic_messages_request always serializes it (anthropic/ns_internal/messages.baml:604-624); test vertex_claude_raw_predict asserts `.model == claude-sonnet-4-5` in the body. The code comment declares this deliberate ("matching both prior Rust implementations"), and sys_llm (build_request/anthropic.rs:119-126) plus the engine did ship it live for years, so it is evidently tolerated today — but it contradicts current docs and is unverifiable live here (no Vertex Claude entitlement on the test project). anthropic_version=vertex-2023-10-16, :rawPredict/:streamRawPredict verbs, body `stream: true` for streaming, and the global-location default all match the docs.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip `model` from the serialized body in the Vertex branch (AnthropicBodyParams could grow an omit_model flag, or the Vertex caller can delete the key via its merge step) to match the documented contract.

findings.claim: Multi-region endpoints (`location: "us"` / `"eu"`) build a nonexistent host `us-aiplatform.googleapis.com` instead of the documented `aiplatform.us.rep.googleapis.com`.
findings.evidence: PROBE probe_vertex_us_multiregion: VertexClient(location="us") → `https://us-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/p/locations/us/...:rawPredict`. Docs (platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-on-vertex-ai, 'Using multi-region endpoints'): `https://aiplatform.${LOCATION}.rep.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/${LOCATION}/...` for LOCATION in {us, eu}. `_vertex_models_base` (ns_internal/vertex.baml:157-161) knows only the `global` and `{location}-aiplatform` host shapes. sys_llm/engine had the same gap (parity), and base_url override is an escape hatch, so minor — but data-residency users following current docs will get a DNS-level NetworkFailure.
findings.suggested_fix: Special-case locations "us" and "eu" to the `aiplatform.{location}.rep.googleapis.com` host in _vertex_models_base.

findings.claim: An express-mode (API key) VertexClient silently switches from the documented project-less endpoint to a project-scoped URL when an ambient GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT/GCLOUD_PROJECT env var is present, because the env chain is consulted before the express short-circuit.
findings.evidence: vertex_project_id (ns_internal/vertex.baml:117-135) checks GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT/GCLOUD_PROJECT before `if (_vertex_is_express(c)) { return null; }`, and _vertex_models_base (:162-168) only falls back to `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/publishers/{publisher}/models` when no project resolved. Express-mode keys are issued for the project-less express endpoint; on GCP runtimes (Cloud Run/GCE set GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT ambiently) the same client instead emits `/v1/projects/{env-project}/locations/{loc}/...?key=...`, which an express key is not authorized for — contradicting the class doc (vertex.baml:16-18 'the request goes to the project-less global endpoint unless a project is configured'; ambient env is not configuration of this client). Could not verify the API's actual rejection behavior live (no express key in Infisical); flagged UNVERIFIED on the wire outcome, but the URL divergence is deterministic from code.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the `_vertex_is_express` null-return above the env-var lookups in vertex_project_id (explicit `project_id` option still wins), so only deliberate configuration selects the project-scoped express URL.
